blocks.content: A&N Islands is administered directly by the Union Government as a Union Territory without a Legislative Assembly — a structural fact that generates a cluster of frequently tested polity questions distinguishing it from UTs with legislatures (Delhi, Puducherry, J&K).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Constitutional & Administrative Status forms the core governing framework.
Districts & Administrative Divisions organize localized governance and policy execution.
Protective & Special Legal Frameworks offer unique legal protections and statutory privileges.
Strategic & Defence Significance highlights critical national security and defense perspectives.

blocks.content: A&N Islands is a Union Territory administered by the President of India through a Lieutenant Governor (LG), who is the head of the administration; unlike Delhi and Puducherry, A&N has no Legislative Assembly of its own — all legislative and executive power effectively rests with the LG under the supervision of the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India.

As of 2026, the Lieutenant Governor is Admiral (Retd.) Devendra Kumar (D.K.) Joshi, PVSM, AVSM, YSM, NM, VSM — former Chief of the Naval Staff — who has held the post since October 2017, making him one of the longest-serving LGs of the territory. His official residence is Raj Niwas / Lok Niwas, Port Blair.
The territory sends exactly one member to the Lok Sabha (constituency: Andaman & Nicobar Islands, unreserved) and has no representation in the Rajya Sabha.
The judiciary of the islands falls under the jurisdiction of the Calcutta High Court, which has a Circuit Bench sitting at Port Blair.

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Classic distinguishing question: 'Which UT has NO Legislative Assembly?' — A&N Islands, Chandigarh, Lakshadweep and Ladakh have no assemblies; Delhi, Puducherry, and Jammu & Kashmir do.

items: South Andaman district — HQ Port Blair (also the UT capital); most populous and most developed district.
North & Middle Andaman district — HQ Mayabunder; created in 2006 by bifurcating the erstwhile Andaman district.
Nicobar district — HQ Car Nicobar; the only district comprising the entire Nicobar group of islands, largely tribal-populated and under Restricted Area Permit (RAP) protection.

blocks.content: The three districts are further divided into tehsils (9 tehsils across the UT as per recent reorganisation) and administered locally through a three-tier Panchayati Raj structure and a Municipal Council for Port Blair town.

blocks.content: Because of the presence of highly vulnerable tribal groups, large parts of the territory are governed by special protective regulations distinct from mainland administrative law — an important and frequently tested distinguishing feature of A&N polity.

items: Andaman & Nicobar Islands (Protection of Aboriginal Tribes) Regulation, 1956 (ANPATR) — the primary legal instrument protecting tribal land, restricting entry into tribal reserves, and regulating photography/filming of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs).

Restricted Area Permit (RAP) — required for foreign nationals to visit most parts of the islands (abolished for many tourist areas in recent years but still applies to tribal reserve zones and the Nicobar district).

North Sentinel Island is legally out of bounds to all visitors under the Foreigners (Protected Areas) Order and ANPATR; the Sentinelese have no contact with the outside world and any unauthorised entry is a punishable offence.

The Andaman & Nicobar Islands (Protection of Aboriginal Tribes) Regulation was significantly amended in 2012 to prohibit the 'human safari' phenomenon along the Andaman Trunk Road through the Jarawa Tribal Reserve.

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: ANPATR 1956 and its 2012 amendment (anti-'human safari' provision protecting the Jarawa) is one of the most exam-relevant polity-cum-tribal-welfare linkages for A&N — remember it links Chapters 3 and 5.

items: Focus on the Constitutional & Administrative Status for polity and governance questions.
Pay special attention to the protective provisions outlined in Special Legal Frameworks.
Note the Strategic & Defence Significance regarding national security directives.

blocks.content: A&N Islands host the Andaman & Nicobar Command (ANC), headquartered at Port Blair — India's first and only tri-service (Army, Navy, Air Force) unified theatre command, established on 8 October 2001, commanded by a Commander-in-Chief (CINCAN) on a rotational basis among the three services.

The islands' location astride the Malacca Strait choke-point — through which a large share of world shipping and China's energy imports pass — gives India significant strategic leverage in the Indo-Pacific and Bay of Bengal region, feeding into India's 'Act East Policy' and Indo-Pacific maritime strategy.
INS Kardip, INS Jarawa and Air Force Station Car Nicobar are among key defence installations in the territory.

items: A&N Islands = UT with NO Legislative Assembly; administered by an LG appointed by the President.
Current LG (2026): Admiral D.K. Joshi (Retd.), in office since 8 October 2017.
1 Lok Sabha seat (unreserved); current MP (since 2024): Bishnu Pada Ray (BJP).
Judicially under Calcutta High Court (Circuit Bench, Port Blair).
3 districts: South Andaman (HQ Port Blair), North & Middle Andaman (HQ Mayabunder), Nicobar (HQ Car Nicobar).
ANPATR 1956 protects tribal reserves; North Sentinel Island is legally off-limits to all visitors.
Andaman & Nicobar Command (ANC), HQ Port Blair — India's only tri-service unified theatre command, est. 2001.
